breaking.headline: Oil plunges about 5% as U.S. stockpiles jump 5.28 million barrels
breaking.fact: U.S. crude stockpiles jumped 5.28 million barrels in the week to Nov. 13, the American Petroleum Institute reported, and oil futures slid about 5% in Wednesday trade even as U.S.–Iran strikes around the strait continued. Both benchmarks are on pace for monthly declines of roughly 20%.

breaking.headline: Nvidia’s earnings pop fizzles as shares slide intraday
breaking.fact: Nvidia jumped nearly 4% after hours Tuesday on a $115.8 billion quarter and a $130 billion Q4 guide, then gave it all back: shares opened higher Wednesday and slid to about 2% lower by midday as the AI selloff resumed, with the Dow down more than 400 points intraday.

breaking.headline: Retail splits three ways: TJX jumps 10%, Target up 6%, Lowe’s slides
breaking.fact: TJX jumped 10% after the off-price retailer beat sales estimates at $15.95 billion with comparable sales up 4%, and Target rose nearly 6% on its best sales growth in five years — comps up 5.6% on a 5% traffic jump — while Lowe’s slid after trimming its operating-margin outlook despite a beat.

breaking.headline: UK inflation hits 3.6%, a 12-month high
breaking.fact: Britain’s consumer price inflation rose to 3.6% in October, its highest in a year and the fourth straight monthly increase, driven by motor fuel — diesel hit a record 199.5p a litre — and tobacco duty. The Bank of England, which raised Bank Rate to 4% this month, expects inflation to peak near 5% next year.

weekInBrief.headline: Housing starts jump 9.9% in October, but permits plunge to a 2020 low
weekInBrief.body: U.S. housing starts jumped 9.9% in October to a 1.309 million annual rate, beating the 1.25 million consensus and ending a three-month slide, the Census Bureau said Wednesday. But building permits — the pipeline for future construction — plunged 7.4% to 1.295 million, the lowest since 2020, and homebuilder sentiment sits at its lowest since 2012.

weekInBrief.headline: Retail sales edge up 0.2% as import prices jump 1.1%
weekInBrief.body: October retail sales rose 0.2%, with the control group that feeds GDP up 0.6% against a 0.3% forecast and sales excluding autos and gasoline up 0.5% — the consumer is still spending. Import prices jumped 1.1%, well above the 0.7% forecast, keeping pressure on the Fed ahead of Wednesday’s minutes.

weekInBrief.headline: Gold breaks below $3,800, a 14-month low
weekInBrief.body: Gold broke below $3,800 an ounce on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025, a 14-month low and more than 30% below January’s record above $5,400, as a firm dollar, 10-year yields above 5% and near-certain December rate-hike bets drained the safe-haven trade; silver sank under $46.

weekInBrief.headline: Salesforce slides 9.45% as AI-displacement fears hammer software
weekInBrief.body: Salesforce fell 9.45% on Tuesday as AI-displacement fears hammered software stocks — RH dropped 8.4% and Intuit 7.2% — helping drag the Dow down 849 points for its worst session in three weeks. Every S&P 500 sector finished red, while gold was flat at $3,851.90 an ounce.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Fresh Iranian drone waves aimed at military installations in Bahrain and Kuwait were intercepted overnight and into Wednesday by air defenses in both countries, after U.S. jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island on Tuesday. U.S. Central Command dismissed Tehran’s claim that six tankers caught fire after striking naval mines in the past 48 hours as psychological warfare, saying the southern transit corridors are mine-free under coalition escort, while Qatar announced a new round of talks with Iranian officials and warned of “grave danger” to diplomacy. On oil, the blockade still holds — UANI’s Nov. 16 update says no Iranian crude tanker has evaded it since July 14, while flows through the strait itself averaged about 8.6 million barrels a day in the week to Nov. 17, down from about 13.5 million in early November, per the independent Hormuz Strait Tracker, and Kpler puts total Gulf exports at about 11 million barrels a day as of Nov. 16.

space.headline: Senate rejects NASA science cuts, blocks closure of 53 missions
space.body: The Senate Appropriations Committee’s fiscal 2027 NASA bill proposes $24.874 billion for the agency, with science funded at $7.43 billion — about 2.5% more than this year, against the White House’s request of $3.9 billion — and explicitly rejects the plan to shut down 53 science missions, including Earth observers Terra, Aqua and Aura and commitments to Europe’s LISA and the Rosalind Franklin rover. The bill is still only a committee recommendation, with a stopgap funding the government until Dec. 11.

space.headline: NASA’s SkyFall Mars helicopters tied to untested nuclear rocket
space.body: NASA is accelerating SkyFall, a mission that would send three small Ingenuity-style helicopters to Mars aboard its Space Reactor-1 Freedom spacecraft — the agency’s first fission-powered interplanetary vehicle — slated to launch in late 2028, fly past Mars in 2029 and return in 2030 to release the helicopters. Former Mars program director Scott Hubbard has questioned pairing the two high-profile efforts, and the project scientist says the helicopters could still fly on a Falcon 9 if the nuclear rocket is not ready.

space.headline: Britain’s first Roman capital was surprisingly diverse
space.body: Chemical analysis of cremated remains from 22 burials in Roman Colchester — Camulodunum, Britain’s first Roman capital — shows several people buried there grew up far outside Britain, with three carrying signatures pointing to childhoods in Mediterranean regions such as Italy, Spain or Lebanon. The Durham University team, combining strontium and lead isotope analysis for the first time on Romano-British cremations, says the findings paint a picture of a diverse population settling in Roman Britain around 2,000 years ago.

space.headline: A quantum microscope reads ten atomic spin states at once
space.body: Researchers at the Institute of Photonic Sciences in Spain have developed a way to identify ten distinct spin states of individual strontium-87 atoms within a single experimental run, a step toward reading out quantum information more completely. The work, announced Nov. 17 and published in Physical Review X, uses a quantum microscope to distinguish the atoms’ internal states one by one.

apod.title: Sierra Snow Season Spins Up
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using MODIS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE and GIBS/Worldview — NASA Earth Observatory Image of the Day, November 18, 2026
apod.explanation: California’s Sierra Nevada got an early taste of wintry weather when one of the first major snowfalls of the water year arrived on November 13, 2026. Nearly 12 inches of snow fell at Donner Pass, northwest of Lake Tahoe, and the MODIS instrument on NASA’s Terra satellite captured this view of the fresh snow on the morning of November 14. More wet weather and mountain snow are forecast, with a winter storm warning in effect November 18–20 and up to 4 feet possible above 8,000 feet.
